providers.notes: A genuinely separate route from the quota, run by the Association of Global Universities with the Ministry of Science and Higher Education since 2017, with NO nationality restriction found. Tracks: bachelor's (16-23), master's (20-33), doctoral (22-35), postdoctoral (24-39). Winners get free tuition in English- or Russian-taught programmes. 2026 cycle verified: registration 20 August-1 November 2026, Stage 1 portfolio to 13 November, Stage 2 to 21 December, Stage 3 interviews to 26 February 2027.

providers.name: Nigeria-Russia bilateral allocation (~220 seats/year)
providers.notes: Nigeria-specific and confirmed on Nigeria's own Federal Ministry of Information site: Russia has offered to raise Nigeria's annual quota above the existing 220. Cross-checked against reporting of a June 2025 Abuja briefing where the Russian Ambassador stated grant packages include tuition, living expenses and travel, with roughly 2,000 Nigerians currently studying in Russia. No self-serve portal for this layer — it runs through Federal Ministry of Education / Russian Embassy nomination. Exact 2026/27 numbers UNVERIFIED.

providers.name: HSE (Higher School of Economics) — quota admission
providers.notes: VERIFIED, and carries a constraint applicants should know before committing: 'HSE has the right to independently determine the programme, regardless of the wishes and priorities of the applicant', and admission to English-taught programmes is restricted for quota admits. Stage 1 opened 15 September. HSE explicitly provides no advisory support for this pathway — everything goes through the national Rossotrudnichestvo office.

providers.name: Saint Petersburg Mining University — quota admission guide
providers.notes: Confirms the quota is allocated by Rossotrudnichestvo with a Stage-1 embassy screening deadline of 1 November — the same date found on HSE's page, indicating a fixed government-wide calendar rather than per-university dates. Also notes admitted students 'can only transfer among programmes within the scope of their subject area', a real constraint if the assigned field is not the applicant's first choice.

providers.name: RUDN University
providers.notes: Structurally significant: founded in 1960 as Patrice Lumumba Peoples' Friendship University specifically to educate students from Africa, Asia and Latin America, and still one of Russia's largest hosts of African students. Participates in Open Doors as an admitting university. A Soviet-era legacy channel that is effectively invisible on Western scholarship aggregators.

providers.name: No national scholarship body — each university funds its own
providers.notes: CONFIRMED by direct fetch, settling the earlier assumption. studyinsaudi.sa identifies itself as 'the official Ministry of Education platform for international students', registered with Saudi Arabia's Digital Government Authority — but it is an application FRONT-END, not a funder: 'After submission, the application is forwarded to the selected educational institution for review.' Unlike China's CSC or Turkiye's YTB, no single body both selects and funds. Each university runs and funds its own programme.

providers.name: Religious and field-of-study constraints at the Islamic universities
providers.notes: Recorded plainly and neutrally because it is a real eligibility constraint applicants should know before investing effort. Saudi Arabia's dedicated Islamic-sciences universities (IU Madinah, IMSIU, and Umm Al-Qura's Sharia colleges) are widely understood to restrict their core scholarship tracks to Muslim applicants and to Islamic-studies or Arabic fields, and IU Madinah's residential scholarship has historically been understood to be male-only. NONE of this was found in quotable text on the official pages that fetched successfully — their deeper eligibility pages 404'd or required a JS-rendered portal — so all of it is UNVERIFIED-FROM-SOURCE and must be confirmed from each university's admission regulations. By contrast the STEM universities (KFUPM, KAUST, KAU) show no such restriction on their official scholarship pages.

providers.name: Islamic Development Bank (IsDB) Scholarship Programmes
providers.notes: MAJOR AFRICA-RELEVANT FIND, headquartered in Jeddah and easily missed because it is a multilateral bank rather than a university or ministry. Three verified tracks: the Scholarship Program for Muslim Communities (undergraduate, from 1983), the M.Sc. Scholarship Program (from 1998) and the Merit Scholarship Program (PhD and post-doctoral, from 1992, focused on applied science and high technology). Covers both member countries and Muslim communities in non-member countries; NIGERIA IS AN IsDB MEMBER COUNTRY, so it qualifies under the member-country track. The 2024-2025 window had closed with 2026-2027 dates not yet published — UNVERIFIED, re-check.

providers.name: King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals (KFUPM)
providers.notes: THE BEST-DOCUMENTED SAUDI OPTION, fully verified from the official page. Undergraduate: tuition 'completely waived for international students outside Saudi Arabia', plus free on-campus housing, free textbooks and a monthly stipend. Graduate: free tuition for PhD and selected MS programmes, stipend by scholarship category, free furnished air-conditioned housing, international airfare, medical and dental care, conference funding and textbooks. Paid research-assistant tracks also exist. No religion or gender restriction stated — a secular STEM university.

providers.name: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST)
providers.notes: VERIFIED: 'Over 90% of admitted students receive full tuition support, a monthly stipend, housing, medical coverage, and relocation assistance' for MS and PhD students — funding is the norm but is not formally guaranteed to 100% of admits. Fully English-taught, secular STEM research university. The KAUST Global Fellowship (kgfp.kaust.edu.sa) is a related named track.

providers.name: Islamic University of Madinah
providers.notes: HISTORICALLY A MAJOR DESTINATION FOR NIGERIAN STUDENTS, though that specific claim traces to Nigerian scholarship press rather than IU's own site and is UNVERIFIED. What IS verified from the official page: a distinct 'Scholarship Student Admission' track separate from domestic admission, open for the 1448H academic year through 29/06/2026, explicitly distinguishing domestic and international scholarships. GAP: the page did not state gender restriction, religion requirement or funding amount in readable form (heavily JavaScript-driven; sub-pages 404'd). Commonly reported but NOT verified: Muslim applicants only, Islamic-sciences focus, and a historically male-only residential programme. Re-verify via IU's admission regulations or care@iu.edu.sa before publishing as fact.

providers.name: King Abdulaziz University (KAU)
providers.notes: Genuinely international in scale — the official homepage confirms over 100,000 students from 100 countries across 33 faculties and 419 programmes. GAP: the homepage surfaced no scholarship eligibility, funding amounts or application process, and the deeper admission page 404'd to automated fetch. Scholarship terms UNVERIFIED pending a successful fetch or direct enquiry.

providers.name: King Saud University (KSU)
providers.notes: The official page directs international applicants to two internal offices (Office of International Students at isd.ksu.edu.sa, and Deanship of Student Affairs) but carries no scholarship eligibility or funding detail itself. UNVERIFIED pending a fetch of isd.ksu.edu.sa.

providers.name: Umm Al-Qura University (UQU), Makkah
providers.notes: Hosts roughly 2,000 international students among 57,000+ total across 30 colleges, and points to its own admission portal and the national Study In Saudi portal — but surfaced no scholarship-specific eligibility or funding text. Its Makkah location makes it a plausible route for Islamic-studies applicants, but that framing is inference rather than a verified claim. UNVERIFIED.

providers.name: Imam Muhammad ibn Saud Islamic University (IMSIU)
providers.notes: A specialist Islamic-sciences and Sharia university comparable in mission to IU Madinah. The homepage is reachable but surfaced no scholarship or international-admission content in this pass. UNVERIFIED — follow up via the site's own contact links before recording eligibility or funding.

providers.name: How scholarships work in Brazil — read this first
providers.notes: STRUCTURAL POINT: Brazilian PUBLIC universities (federal and state) charge NO tuition to anyone, including international students. So a Brazilian 'bolsa' is usually a monthly living stipend, not a tuition waiver — the funding question is living costs, and the tuition question mostly disappears. Separately: PROUNI and FIES, the two programmes most often surfaced by search, are for BRAZILIAN students at private universities only and are NOT open to international applicants.

providers.name: ACCESS WARNING — gov.br and gcub.org.br block automated fetching
providers.notes: Checked 2026-09-05: gov.br/capes returned HTTP 401, gov.br/mec served a CAPTCHA, agenciagov.ebc.com.br is disallowed by robots.txt, and gcub.org.br returned 403/timeouts. Every Brazilian federal row below is therefore HUMAN-READ ONLY — same handling as Oxford, Westminster, Melbourne and ng.usembassy.gov. Do not point a fetcher at them or add them to RECHECK_TARGETS; a person must open the page and read the deadline.

providers.name: CAPES Move Africa — HIGH-PRIORITY LEAD, needs human verification
providers.notes: POTENTIALLY THE MOST RELEVANT ROW IN THIS ENTIRE SHEET FOR TALENTRAH. Announced May 2026: a CAPES programme reported as offering ~2,600 master's and doctoral scholarships specifically for AFRICAN students at Brazilian institutions. UNVERIFIED — every figure here comes from search-result headlines and Brazilian press, and the official CAPES page returned HTTP 401 to an honest fetch, so nothing here has been read from the source. Whether Nigeria is among the eligible countries is NOT established. Worth a human opening this page early, given the size of the programme and its explicit Africa focus.

providers.name: PEC-G — Programa de Estudantes-Convenio de Graduacao
providers.notes: Ministry of Foreign Affairs UNDERGRADUATE programme for nationals of developing countries with which Brazil holds an education agreement — includes several African countries. Portuguese proficiency generally required (Celpe-Bras). Human-read only, see access warning above.

providers.name: PEC-PG — Programa de Estudante-Convenio de Pos-Graduacao
providers.notes: POSTGRADUATE equivalent of PEC-G (master's/doctorate), run jointly by MRE with CAPES and CNPq, same developing-country agreement basis. Human-read only.

providers.name: CAPES (Coordenacao de Aperfeicoamento de Pessoal de Nivel Superior)
providers.notes: Federal graduate-education agency — the single largest funder of master's/doctoral stipends in Brazil. Co-administers PEC-PG and runs Move Africa. Human-read only.

providers.name: CNPq (Conselho Nacional de Desenvolvimento Cientifico e Tecnologico)
providers.notes: Federal research-funding council; funds graduate and research stipends, co-administers PEC-PG. Human-read only.

providers.name: CNPq ProAfrica
providers.notes: CNPq's Brazil-Africa cooperation line; a 2026 call for joint Brazil-Africa scientific projects was reported open. Funds RESEARCH PROJECTS and associated mobility rather than open student scholarships — check whether a given call carries student stipends before treating it as a scholarship.

providers.name: GCUB — Grupo de Cooperacao Internacional de Universidades Brasileiras
providers.notes: Consortium of Brazilian universities that administers several international scholarship programmes jointly with CAPES and other partners (see GCUB-Mob below). Site returned 403/timeouts to an honest fetch on 2026-09-05 — human-read only.

providers.name: GCUB-Mob — GCUB International Mobility Program
providers.notes: LEAD, needs human verification. Master's and doctoral scholarships at Brazilian universities for international students; a 5th-edition call (No. 001/2026) was visible in search results. The eligible-country list is NOT verified — do not assume African or Nigerian eligibility without reading the call. Site 403s automated access.

providers.name: PAEC OEA-GCUB — EXCLUDED on the eligibility rule
providers.notes: CHECKED AND EXCLUDED 2026-09-05. Confirmed on a host university's own page (UFJF): the programme is for 'students from 34 OAS member countries, except Brazil' — Organization of American States members only. Nigeria and African countries are NOT eligible. Same exclusion rule that removed Manaaki NZ and ADB-JSP from Talentrah's catalog. Recorded here so nobody re-adds it: the name looks pan-international, the eligibility is not.

providers.name: CONFAP — Conselho Nacional das Fundacoes Estaduais de Amparo a Pesquisa
providers.notes: Umbrella body for Brazil's 26+ STATE research foundations (FAPs). This English page lists every state agency in one place — the efficient way to reach FAPERJ, FAPESB, FACEPE, FAPESC, FAPEAM and the rest without chasing each separately. State FAPs are a large and commonly-missed layer of Brazilian funding.

providers.name: FAPESP — Fundacao de Amparo a Pesquisa do Estado de Sao Paulo
providers.notes: The largest and best-funded state research foundation in Brazil (Sao Paulo). Funds master's, doctoral and post-doctoral scholarships in Brazil; several lines are open to foreign researchers hosted at Sao Paulo institutions.

providers.name: FAPEMIG — Fundacao de Amparo a Pesquisa do Estado de Minas Gerais
providers.notes: State research foundation for Minas Gerais; funds research and graduate stipends.

providers.name: FAPERGS — Fundacao de Amparo a Pesquisa do Estado do Rio Grande do Sul
providers.notes: State research foundation for Rio Grande do Sul; funds scientific-initiation and graduate stipends.

providers.name: Santander Open Academy (Bolsas/Becas Santander)
providers.notes: Large private bank-funded scholarship programme with a substantial Brazilian footprint, delivered in partnership with individual universities. Mix of study, language and mobility grants; eligibility is usually set per-call and per-partner-university.

providers.name: Universidade de Sao Paulo (USP)
providers.notes: Brazil's largest and highest-ranked university. International Cooperation Office runs exchange and scholarship programmes; public, so no tuition.

providers.name: Universidade Estadual de Campinas (UNICAMP)
providers.notes: Major Sao Paulo state research university; International Relations Office handles incoming international students.

providers.name: Universidade de Brasilia (UnB)
providers.notes: Federal university in the capital; dedicated international-students portal covering admission routes for foreigners.

providers.name: Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro (UFRJ)
providers.notes: Large federal university with an English-language 'Study at UFRJ' section for international applicants.

providers.name: Universidade Federal de Minas Gerais (UFMG)
providers.notes: Federal university; Office of International Affairs (DRI) publishes an international-student guide and mobility routes.

providers.name: Universidade Federal de Sao Carlos (UFSCar)
providers.notes: Notable because its graduate office maintains a page specifically for master's/doctoral scholarships in Brazil reserved for FOREIGN candidates — a useful model page for finding which programmes a given Brazilian university actually participates in.

providers.name: Universidade Federal de Juiz de Fora (UFJF)
providers.notes: International office publishes clear English-language pages on each incoming-scholarship programme it participates in; this was the source that established PAEC OEA-GCUB's OAS-only eligibility.

providers.name: Many 'global' fellowships fund a seat, not an application
providers.notes: RECURRING STRUCTURAL FINDING worth acting on. The biggest-sounding global names — WHO/TDR, most UNESCO co-sponsored fellowships, several DAAD in-region tracks — are not single-portal programmes. The funding body explicitly does not process admissions; the applicant must first be independently admitted by a specific named partner university, and the funding then attaches. So 'apply to WHO' or 'apply to UNESCO' is usually the wrong instruction; 'get admitted to [named partner university], then apply for the named funding' is correct.

providers.name: Pan African University (PAU) — African Union funded
providers.notes: AFRICA-HOSTED AND AFRICA-FUNDED, and routinely absent from Western scholarship lists. Run by the African Union: 'The African Union Commission will offer full scholarships to successful candidates', delivered across PAU institutes physically located in Africa. Open to applicants 'from African countries and the Diaspora' for master's and PhD. Note the gender-differentiated age caps: master's max 25 (male) / 28 (female); PhD max 28 (male) / 30 (female). The 2026-2027 deadline was 15 December 2025.

providers.name: Islamic Development Bank — Member Countries track
providers.notes: Nigeria is a confirmed IsDB Member Country, so it qualifies for the member-country track including the Merit Scholarship Programme (PhD and post-doctoral, high-technology focus). The 2024-2025 cycle is confirmed closed and no consolidated 2026-2027 deadline was published on the main page — verify via isdbscholarships.smartsimple.com before advising anyone.

providers.name: IsDB-ISFD Least Developed Member Countries track — EXCLUDES Nigeria
providers.notes: A SUBTLE EXCLUSION inside an otherwise open funder. The official booklet lists 21 eligible least-developed member countries by name: 'Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Benin, Burkina Faso, Chad, Comoros, Djibouti, Gambia, Guinea, Guinea Bissau, Mali, Mauritania, Mozambique, Niger, Senegal, Sierra Leone, Somalia, Sudan, Togo, Uganda, and Yemen.' Nigeria is NOT among them — so a Nigerian is excluded from this specific track while remaining eligible under IsDB's general member-country track above. Exactly the kind of distinction that wastes an applicant's time if missed.

providers.name: Commonwealth Scholarships routed via Nigeria's Federal Scholarship Board
providers.notes: THE MECHANIC NIGERIAN APPLICANTS MOST OFTEN GET WRONG. Applications from Nigeria are NOT made directly to the CSC — they are administered by Nigeria's Federal Scholarship Board (fsb@education.gov.ng), which requires at least two UK university admissions, an NYSC discharge or exemption certificate, and a first-class or second-class-upper degree for master's applicants. The 2025/2026 cycle ran 2 September-14 October 2025; expect a similarly timed call.

providers.name: UNESCO Fellowships — an umbrella of ~10 separate donor schemes
providers.notes: IMPORTANT CLARIFICATION: UNESCO does not run one unified fellowship. It hosts separate donor-funded schemes with different rules — UNESCO/China Great Wall (75 places), TWAS PhD (160), OWSD PhD, UNESCO/Russia-ISEDC (20), UNESCO/Japan Keizo Obuchi, UNESCO/Poland Engineering (28) and Archaeology (7), UNESCO/Korea (25), UNESCO/Saudi AlUla (10), UNESCO/Nestle (20). Keizo Obuchi's cycle deadline was confirmed as 30 September 2026. Eligibility varies per sub-programme and was NOT individually verified — check each separately.

providers.name: WHO/TDR Postgraduate Training Scheme
providers.notes: Open to researchers from low- and middle-income countries via seven partner universities, with African partners in Ghana, South Africa and Zambia named on the page. Funds 'full time tuition and board, cost of dissertation research/field work, return air travel from home country to institution and contribution towards textbooks'. CRITICAL MECHANIC, quoted: 'TDR will not receive or process applications or enquiries about admissions' — win admission to the partner university first, then apply for the funded seat.

providers.name: IAEA Marie Sklodowska-Curie Fellowship Programme
providers.notes: WOMEN-ONLY master's scholarship in nuclear-related fields, with 'geographic and linguistic diversity' cited as a selection factor and no nationality bar found. Funds master's tuition and costs plus a small number of competitive internship placements. Most recent confirmed deadline was 31 October 2025 — check for the next cycle.

providers.name: FAO-Hungary Government Scholarship Programme
providers.notes: A genuinely obscure but real option: a joint FAO / Hungarian government programme delivered through Hungary's Ministry of Agriculture, explicitly open to 43 named countries INCLUDING NIGERIA, Ghana, Kenya, Ethiopia and Uganda. Funds tuition, dormitory, subsistence and health insurance for named master's programmes (Agricultural Biotechnology at Godollo; Animal Nutrition and Feed Safety Engineering at Kaposvar). The 2026-27 window was 21 January-28 February 2026 — useful for planning next year's cycle.

providers.name: DAAD In-Country/In-Region Programme (hosted at African universities)
providers.notes: Funds master's and PhD study physically hosted at partner universities inside the student's own region, with Sub-Saharan Africa a priority region (Eastern Africa and West/Central Africa calls cited). Nigeria was NOT explicitly named in the fetched page content — Nigeria-specific eligibility is UNVERIFIED; confirm via the current call text or a named host university.

providers.name: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program
providers.notes: Confirmed still active — partner-university pages (e.g. Cambridge) state 'Applications for the 2026/2027 academic year are now open'. Delivered through partner universities in Africa and worldwide, funding the full cost of study plus leadership and mentorship components. Apply through the specific partner university, never centrally. Already live in Talentrah's catalog.

providers.name: Rotary Peace Fellowships
providers.notes: Up to 170 fully funded fellowships per year (max 50 master's, 120 professional-development certificate) across eight Rotary Peace Centers worldwide, covering tuition, fees, room and board, round-trip travel and field-study costs. No nationality restriction found. TIMING: the 2027-28 cycle is closed and the next opens February 2027.

providers.name: Carnegie African Diaspora Fellowship Program — winding down
providers.notes: Africa-hosted in six countries INCLUDING NIGERIA (with Ghana, Kenya, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda). IMPORTANT SCOPE LIMIT: it funds African-BORN academics already on faculty at US or Canadian universities to do short project stays at African host institutions — NOT prospective students seeking a degree. The official page confirms the programme is in its 'final phase' (2013-2025), transitioning to an alumni-network model. Treat as winding down.

providers.name: Open Society Foundations — individual scholarships largely wound down
providers.notes: VERIFY BEFORE CHASING. The official grants page lists only one open individual opportunity (the Open Society Fellowship, for public intellectuals, already past deadline) and states 'the vast majority of our grants are awarded to organizations that we approach directly'. OSF's historic dedicated Africa and Central Asia individual scholarship schemes are absent from the current opportunities page — treat any aggregator claiming an open OSF student scholarship as needing direct re-verification.

providers.name: Agence universitaire de la Francophonie (AUF) — Nigeria eligibility doubtful
providers.notes: Confirmed real and active: AUF groups 1,007 institutions across 119 countries and runs dozens of open calls. However, the official pages did NOT confirm whether Nigeria has member universities or whether Nigerian nationals at non-member institutions can apply, and Nigeria is not a Francophonie member state — so eligibility is doubtful by default. Do not list AUF as open to Nigerians without a specific call naming Nigeria or an eligible host university. See also the AUF Eugene Ionesco exclusion recorded under France.

providers.name: Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program (JJ/WBGSP)
providers.notes: Already live in Talentrah's catalog. Two annual application windows; exact dates are published inside the application guidelines PDF rather than on the landing page, which is why this listing carries a deadline note rather than a date.

providers.name: MEXT Japanese Government Scholarship
providers.notes: Already live in Talentrah's catalog. Deadlines are delegated to the applicant's local Japanese embassy, so there is no single global date — the Abuja embassy sets Nigeria's.

Per Talentrah's standing rule, every deadline, eligibility and funding fact must be confirmed on the provider's own official page. This pass produced repeated proof of why: Ontario Trillium, Ford IFP and several Wellcome schemes are all still listed as open by aggregators years after officially closing.
